deutsche-lpm.title: Curriculum as a computable, versioned knowledge system, not a static document set

content.label: Curriculum as a computable, versioned knowledge system, not a static document set
content.statement: A Lehrplan revision should produce more than an updated set of PDF documents: it should produce (or be accompanied by) a machine- readable representation of competencies, concepts, prerequisites, and cross-subject relationships, versioned and queryable, so that questions like "where is concept X taught," "what depends on what," and "where is content duplicated or missing a prerequisite" can be answered computationally rather than by manual document review.
content.rationale: Germany already has partial infrastructure for exactly this shape of representation -- FWU's public MEM Lehrplan ontology has live, queryable data for four Bundesländer today, and Saxony's own Dynamische Lehrplandatenbank already links Lehrplan documents to materials and curricular analyses. The gap is not "should curriculum become data" -- some of it already is -- but extending that representation to genuinely support cross-subject/competency-level analysis, not just document/material lookup.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed. Grounding is real (a confirmed crosswalk record), but the principle statement itself is an OpenEvo position, not a verified external fact.

deutsche-lpm.title: Machine-readable curriculum data should be extended and treated as public infrastructure

content.label: Machine-readable curriculum data should be extended and treated as public infrastructure
content.statement: Where a state ministry or federal body already publishes machine-readable curriculum data (as FWU's MEM ontology does for four Länder today), that data's coverage should be extended -- more subjects, more Länder, competency/Lernziel-level granularity, not just document-level metadata -- and its existence should be treated as a public good that research groups and tool-builders can build on, not an incidental byproduct of one institute's internal tooling.
content.rationale: The value of a curriculum knowledge graph compounds with coverage: cross-subject and cross-Land comparison is only possible once enough states/subjects are represented in a compatible way. Today's four-Land, mostly-document-level coverage is a real start, not yet sufficient for the kind of coherence analysis this repo's CCS domain is aimed at.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: Curriculum meta-modelling as public knowledge infrastructure for the policy-practice gap

content.label: Curriculum meta-modelling as public knowledge infrastructure for the policy-practice gap
content.statement: The space between a Lehrplan's stated Lernziele and what actually happens in classrooms is populated by teacher and researcher knowledge and belief that mostly stays tacit -- how a competency is actually interpreted, which prerequisites a Fachdidaktik group believes matter, where "the same" curriculum is understood differently across schools. Building explicit, machine-readable curriculum meta-models -- and treating them as open public infrastructure rather than a proprietary tool -- makes that landscape visible and contestable, which is the actual precondition for participatory curriculum improvement, not merely its output.
content.rationale: A curriculum-policy process that only ever produces revised documents (however good) re-hides this gap every cycle -- the tacit knowledge that shaped the last revision has to be rediscovered for the next one. An open meta-model persists that knowledge in queryable form across revision cycles, which is a different and larger claim than "curriculum data should be machine-readable" (DELP-PRINCIPLE-curriculum-as-computable-system) -- that principle is about representing the curriculum; this one is about representing the community's evolving understanding of it.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle synthesizing the user's own framing (2026-08-23 conversation) of curriculum meta-modelling as the public-knowledge-infrastructure answer to the policy/practice gap. Not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: Support a networked ecosystem of Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, with CCS as shared methodology

content.label: Support a networked ecosystem of Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, with CCS as shared methodology
content.statement: Germany's Fachdidaktik research capacity is real but organized subject-by-subject, largely siloed across university teacher-education programmes. Rather than proposing a new central authority, a supportive ecosystem should network existing Fach-specific Didaktik research groups, and should support a new kind of interdisciplinary didactic research group organized around cross-cutting questions rather than a single Schulfach. Computational Curriculum Studies' role in that ecosystem is to be methodological glue and shared toolkit -- common curriculum representations and analysis methods usable by any participating group -- not a replacement for subject-specific expertise.
content.rationale: This ecosystem already has a concrete, if not yet funded, test of exactly this kind of relationship: KoMet ("Kohärenz durch Meta-Modellierung von Curricula"), a BMBFSFJ grant proposal in development (KoMet repo, target: Modul C "Digitale Souveränität", not yet a published call as of 2026-08-23) that would formalize a Verbund across four real Fachdidaktik groups -- Jena (lead, PI Dr. Susan Hanisch), Halle (Jun.-Prof. Dr. Christopher Hempel), Kassel (Dr. Tim Hartelt), and Bamberg (Prof. Dr. Alexander Bergmann-Gering) -- with OpenEvo CCS infrastructure (ConceptBase, curriculum-agents) as the shared methodological layer its own WP1 is built on. This principle generalizes that one live proposal into an explicit policy stance about what should exist regardless of whether this specific grant succeeds, rather than treating KoMet as a one-off. It also gives interdisciplinary_design's "what does it mean to be human?" framing a concrete institutional form: the "new kind of interdisciplinary didactic research group" this principle calls for is where that framing would actually live organizationally.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle synthesizing the user's own framing (2026-08-23 conversation). Updated same day after reading the KoMet repo directly: what was framed as one unexecuted federation case is, in fact, the exact structure a real (unfunded) grant proposal is already trying to formalize across four institutions -- this principle's rationale now cites that proposal by name rather than a single hypothetical case. Not yet reviewed.

deutsche-lpm.title: A Proposed Biologie/Informatik Bridge: Modeling the Hormone System as an Information-Processing System

content.label: A Proposed Biologie/Informatik Bridge: Modeling the Hormone System as an Information-Processing System

baselineCurriculumObject.subject: Biologie
baselineCurriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: bk_information_kommunikation (one of six real KMK-Basiskonzepte Biologie, Thüringer Lehrplan Biologie Gymnasium Klassen 7-8)
baselineCurriculumObject.excerptText: Real Lernziel content this redesign starts from (EvoMentor_DE/data/kohaerenzfaeden.json, thread kf-002, read directly): GY-78-HUM-FES-1 "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren" and GY-78-HUM-ABW-5 "spezifische Abwehr und Gedächtniszellen" (kf-003) -- both real, existing Klassenstufe-8 Lernziele already tagged bk_information_kommunikation, taught entirely within Biologie today.

theoreticalGrounding.changedCommitment: The real baseline treats Information/Kommunikation as a Biologie-internal Basiskonzept -- real, but with zero structural link to any other subject (confirmed: no Biologie Lernziel in the corpus cross-references Informatik, and DELP-FINDING-informatik-modellieren- convergence's own real Thüringen Informatik data confirms the reverse is also true). This redesign changes exactly one commitment: information processing is treated as the domain- general construct OE-CROSSDOMAINCONSTRUCT-information-processing-domain-general already names, deliberately cross-referenced with Informatik per OE-PROPOSITION-icr-competency-domain-interdependence, rather than left as a Biologie-only Basiskonzept.

proposedRedesign.narrative: Thüringen's real Informatik Lehrplan (Klassenstufen 9/10, Wahlpflichtfach) already teaches that "jedes Informatiksystem als Kombination von Hard- und Software-Komponenten das Ergebnis eines informatischen Modellierungsvorgangs ist" (DELP-FINDING-informatik- modellieren-convergence, primary-source-confirmed) -- a real, named "informatische Modellierung" methodology for representing a system as a formal model before analyzing it. Biologie's real Klassenstufe-8 content already characterizes the hormone system AS an information system (GY-78-HUM-FES-1) and the immune system's antigen-antibody recognition as an information-processing analogue of enzymatic specificity (GY-78-HUM-ABW-5, per kf-003's own Schlüssel-Schloss link). Today these sit in two different subjects, two different grade bands (Kl.8 vs. Kl.9/10), with no structural connection -- exactly the "topic accumulation without explaining why the topics connect" pattern EvoMentor_DE's own basiskonzepte-kohaerenz-strategie.md warns against, now occurring across subjects rather than within one. This redesign proposes a Klassenstufe-9/10 joint unit (co-taught or explicitly cross-referenced between Biologie and Informatik) in which students apply Informatik's own real "informatische Modellierung" methodology to the hormone system they already studied in Biologie Kl.8 -- building a formal model (a state/signal-flow diagram) of hormonal signal transduction, using the same modeling discipline Informatik teaches for designed information systems, then explicitly comparing what is genuinely the same (information encoding, transmission, receiver-side interpretation) and what genuinely differs (no designer, no fixed hardware/software boundary) between a biological and a designed information system.

newOrChangedElements.description: A new Klassenstufe-9/10 joint Lernziel (does not exist today): "Erstellt ein formales Modell (Zustands- oder Signalflussdiagramm) der hormonellen Signalübertragung unter Anwendung der in Informatik erlernten Modellierungsmethodik, und vergleicht es explizit mit einem Modell eines entworfenen Informatiksystems hinsichtlich Kodierung, Übertragung und Interpretation von Information."

A new, explicit cross-reference from Informatik's real "informatische Modellierung" Lernbereich (Kl.9/10) back to the Biologie hormone-system content, framed as "you already built an intuitive model of an information system in Biologie -- now make that modeling process formal and general." No change to Informatik's own real competency content required, only an added cross-reference and a shared worked example.

tradeoffAssessment.gains: Makes OE-CROSSDOMAINCONSTRUCT-information-processing-domain-general's claim curricular reality rather than only theoretical: students encounter the same formal modeling discipline applied to a designed system (Informatik) and a biological one (Biologie) two years after first meeting the biological case informally, which is exactly the "general pattern, encountered again at higher sophistication" structure interdisciplinary-k12's own strand-201/202 substrand-213/224 edits (OE-CURRICULUMDECISION-interdisciplinary-strand- 201-information-cross-reference, -202-...) already operationalize for OE-INTERDISCIPLINARY. Costs no new Informatik content -- the real "informatische Modellierung" competency already exists and already generalizes; this only asks it to be pointed at an example already familiar from Biologie.
tradeoffAssessment.costs: Requires cross-department coordination (Biologie and Informatik are taught by different teachers, often not co-planned) that neither subject's real Lehrplan currently asks for or provides time/structure to support -- a real, non-trivial implementation cost this record does not resolve. Informatik is a Wahlpflichtfach (elective) at Kl.9/10 in Thüringen, so this redesign would only reach students who chose it, not the full Klassenstufe-8 Biologie cohort that met the hormone-system content originally -- a genuine reach limitation, not a universal replacement for the current Biologie-only treatment.

provenance.sourceProvenance: Baseline: EvoMentor_DE/data/basiskonzepte.json (v5.0) and kohaerenzfaeden.json (v1.1, thread kf-002/kf-003), read directly. Informatik convergence: DELP-FINDING-informatik-modellieren-convergence (national_ccs_policy/records/ coherence-findings.yaml), primary-source-confirmed, citing Lehrplan Informatik, Thüringen (2012), https://www.schulportal-thueringen.de/tip/resources/medien/21770. Theoretical grounding: theorybase records added this same 2026-08-26 session (submissions branch, not yet merged to theorybase main).
provenance.contributor_notes: First record under the new synthetic-curriculum-redesign-record schema -- the "adjacent possible" synthetic modeling capacity discussed and scoped this session (see lab_manager/docs/design-notes/fair-theory-rigor-and-synthetic-lpm-discourse-strategic-plan.md §4). Deliberately picked the strongest available real-data anchor (both the Biologie baseline AND the Informatik connection point are primary-source-confirmed real content, not invented) rather than a weaker candidate, since this is the schema's first real instance and should demonstrate the discipline at its best, not its minimum bar.

deutsche-lpm.title: A DCR-Consonant Counterpart: Removing the Incidental Cross-Basiskonzept Threading From Information/Kommunikation

content.label: A DCR-Consonant Counterpart: Removing the Incidental Cross-Basiskonzept Threading From Information/Kommunikation

baselineCurriculumObject.subject: Biologie
baselineCurriculumObject.lernbereichLabel: bk_information_kommunikation (same real baseline as DELP-SYNTHETIC-thueringen-biologie-informatik-information-processing-bridge -- deliberately identical, to hold the starting data constant and vary only the theoretical commitment)
baselineCurriculumObject.excerptText: Same real Lernziel content as the ICR-side counterpart record: GY-78-HUM-FES-1 "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren" and GY-78-HUM-ABW-5 "spezifische Abwehr und Gedächtniszellen" (EvoMentor_DE/data/kohaerenzfaeden.json, kf-002/kf-003, read directly).

theoreticalGrounding.changedCommitment: The real baseline already carries incidental cross-Basiskonzept threading -- kf-002 links Information/Kommunikation to Steuerung/Regelung and individuelle Entwicklung; kf-003 links it to Struktur/Funktion and Stoff-/Energieumwandlung via the shared Schlüssel-Schloss principle -- present in the real data but never taught as deliberate cross-referencing (per EvoMentor_DE's own basiskonzepte-kohaerenz-strategie.md, these are latent co- occurrences, not curricular design). This redesign changes exactly one commitment, the mirror image of the ICR-side record's change: rather than making the latent cross- Basiskonzept threading explicit and deliberate (ICR), treat Information/Kommunikation as a fully self-contained Biologie unit whose mechanistic completeness does not depend on any other Basiskonzept or subject, per OE-PROPOSITION-dcr-competency-domain-independence -- the same choice BIO-CORE's real vocabulary already makes structurally (see OE-CURRICULUMDECISION-bio-core-strand-101-no-information-concept), applied here to a real German curriculum rather than only to an OpenEvo LPM.

proposedRedesign.narrative: Where the ICR-side record proposes a new Kl.9/10 joint unit connecting hormone-system signaling to Informatik's modeling methodology, this redesign proposes the opposite move applied to the same Kl.8 content: strip the "Informationssystem" framing itself from GY-78-HUM-FES-1's real formulation and replace it with a purely physiological framing that makes no appeal to a domain-general information concept at all -- "Beschreibt den hormonellen Regelkreis der Pubertätsentwicklung: Hypothalamus, Hypophyse, Gonaden, deren Wechselwirkung und Rückkopplung" instead of "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren." Similarly, GY-78-HUM-ABW-5's antigen-antibody content would be taught via its own biological specificity mechanism (protein structure, binding-site complementarity) without invoking the Schlüssel-Schloss cross-reference to enzymatic specificity in Stoff-/Energieumwandlung that kf-003 currently makes latent. Both changes are deletions/reframings of existing real content, not additions -- the redesign makes the curriculum MORE narrowly biological, testing whether anything of real instructional value is actually lost by doing so, which is precisely what tradeoffAssessment below is for.

newOrChangedElements.description: Reframe GY-78-HUM-FES-1 from "Hormonsystem als Informationssystem charakterisieren" to a purely physiological formulation naming the hypothalamus-hypophyse-gonaden feedback loop directly, without the domain-general "information system" framing.

Teach GY-78-HUM-ABW-5's antigen-antibody specificity via its own structural-biological mechanism only, without the kf-003 cross-reference to Stoff-/Energieumwandlung's enzymatic Schlüssel-Schloss principle -- each Basiskonzept's Schlüssel-Schloss instance taught and assessed independently within its own unit.

tradeoffAssessment.gains: Tighter within-unit focus and a shorter conceptual-prerequisite chain per topic -- a student does not need the Struktur/Funktion Schlüssel-Schloss content secure before the immune-system unit makes sense on its own terms, matching DCR's own stated virtue (clarity over completeness, OE-ASSUMPTION-dcr-clarity-over-completeness) and reducing the risk kf-003's own real gap note already names: no Gy910 Lernziel currently revisits the Schlüssel-Schloss thread to deepen it, so the cross-reference may currently be introduced and then simply dropped rather than genuinely built on.
tradeoffAssessment.costs: Directly forfeits the real coherence kf-002/kf-003 already document as latent in the actual curriculum -- the hormone-system-as-information-system framing is not an OpenEvo invention layered onto the real Lernziel, it is already implicit in the real Lehrplan language ("Informationssystem" is EvoMentor_DE's own real reading of Klassenstufe-8 content), so removing it is a genuine loss of an already-real explanatory thread, not a neutral simplification. Also forfeits exactly the OE-CROSSDOMAINCONSTRUCT-information- processing-domain-general grounding this whole family of records exists to test -- this redesign is the honest "what if the ICR reading is wrong or premature" control case, not a recommendation.

provenance.sourceProvenance: Same real baseline sources as DELP-SYNTHETIC-thueringen-biologie-informatik-information- processing-bridge (EvoMentor_DE/data/basiskonzepte.json v5.0, kohaerenzfaeden.json v1.1). Theoretical grounding: theorybase records added this session (submissions branch, not yet merged to theorybase main), including OE-CURRICULUMDECISION-bio-core-strand-101-no- information-concept, added the same session specifically to ground this record's DCR counterpart claim in a real, checked fact about BIO-CORE rather than an assertion.
provenance.contributor_notes: Deliberately holds the baseline constant with DELP-SYNTHETIC-thueringen-biologie- informatik-information-processing-bridge and varies only theoreticalGrounding. changedCommitment, so the two records together form a genuine controlled A/B comparison of the same real curriculum content read through DCR's vs. ICR's competency-domain- specificity commitment -- the concrete instance of "depending on how one reads the science... the curriculum design looks very different," per Dustin's own framing of this workstream's purpose (2026-08-26 session).

nys-lpm.title: Introducing OpenEvo's content-anchor and rubric infrastructure to SCDN

nys-lpm.title: "What does it mean to be human?" as a jurisdiction-independent integrating question

content.label: "What does it mean to be human?" as a jurisdiction-independent integrating question
content.statement: Across any graduation framework that names critical thinking, global citizenship, or civic/ethical reasoning as a required competency -- New York's Portrait of a Graduate, or any other state's or country's equivalent -- evolutionary anthropology's integrating question ("what does it mean to be human?") offers a single, scientifically grounded thread connecting content that a standard subject-by-subject curriculum leaves scattered: biology's account of human evolutionary history, psychology's account of cognition and development, economics' and political science's account of cooperation and institutions, and ethics' account of how norms and values emerged and operate. This is the same framing `deutsche_lp`'s own `interdisciplinary_design/` folder states for the German context -- restated here in jurisdiction-independent form specifically so both repos' state/Land-level principles can adaptedFrom the same root rather than each inventing a slightly different version.
content.rationale: A jurisdiction-independent root principle is what makes state-level adaptation ("adaptedFrom") meaningful rather than decorative -- without one, every state-level principle would restate the same framing from scratch, and a future comparison across states (or across the US/Germany boundary) would have nothing common to point at.

provenance.contributor_notes: Adapted directly from deutsche_lp/interdisciplinary_design/README.md's own framing, not independently re-derived -- credited as such rather than presented as a new idea.

nys-lpm.title: New York's Portrait is one instance of a real, named multi-state trend, not a one-off

content.label: New York's Portrait is one instance of a real, named multi-state trend, not a one-off
content.statement: Multiple US states have adopted or are drafting "Portrait of a Graduate"-style frameworks (EdWeek, December 2023, "More States Are Creating a 'Portrait of a Graduate'. Here's Why"). New York's version is distinctive for being unusually binding (tied directly to diploma credit requirements rather than staying an aspirational statement) and unusually fast-moving (Portrait adopted July 2025, escalated to a "first-in-the-nation" competency-based-diploma direction by June 2026), but it is not sui generis. A strategy built for New York should track which pieces are New York-specific (the Regents' binding authority, the specific six attributes, NYSED's specific actors) and which pieces would transfer to another Portrait-adopting state with light adaptation (the underlying content-anchor/evidence-rubric offer), so that a successful New York pilot has a clear path to becoming a template rather than a one-off.
content.rationale: Named explicitly so this repo's later state-level work doesn't have to re-discover that New York is part of a larger pattern -- and so that adding a second state later (see CONTRIBUTING.md § Adding a new state) has a place to record what's actually common across states versus what New York's specific case made easy to overlook as New-York-only.

provenance.contributor_notes: The EdWeek trend claim itself is from a WebSearch result title only (search: "New York State interdisciplinary curriculum design organizations competency-based education Portrait of a Graduate partners") -- the article was not independently WebFetched this session. Verify directly before citing which other specific states have adopted similar frameworks.
provenance.sourceProvenance: WebSearch result: 'More States Are Creating a Portrait of a Graduate. Here's Why', edweek.org/policy-politics/..., December 2023 -- title/existence only, not independently fetched 2026-09-11.

nys-lpm.title: Global Citizen attribute <-> evolved cooperation and the psychology of institutions

content.label: Global Citizen attribute <-> evolved cooperation and the psychology of institutions

curriculumObject.excerptText: "Acts responsibly and ethically in local, global, and digital communities, promoting sustainability and civic engagement." NYKids' own framing (Aaron Leo, 2026-03-10) adds that this requires "more than voting" -- active community participation and critical media literacy.
curriculumObject.sourceDocument: NYSED Portrait of a Graduate framework; NYKids analysis

content.evolutionaryAnthropologyHub: Evolved cooperation psychology and the emergence of large-scale institutions -- specifically, why human cooperation at the scale of strangers (a "global" or "digital" community, in the Portrait's own words) requires evolved mechanisms beyond kin selection and direct reciprocity: reputation systems, third-party punishment of norm violators, and culturally-transmitted institutions that scale cooperation past face-to-face group size. This is the same theoretical territory OpenEvo's Cooperation Games and Governing the Commons content anchors already draw on.
content.connectionNarrative: "Global citizenship" as usually taught risks staying at the level of values instruction (be a good global citizen) without a causal account of why cooperation at scale is hard, fragile, and biologically unusual -- which is exactly the kind of civic cynicism or naive-idealism failure mode NYKids' own "more than voting" framing is trying to head off. Teaching evolved cooperation mechanisms alongside the Global Citizen attribute gives students a mechanistic answer to "why do institutions like courts, elections, or international agreements exist and sometimes fail" rather than only a normative one -- turning "act like a good global citizen" into "understand the real, evolved fragility of large-scale cooperation you're being asked to sustain."

openEvoDesignConcept.justification: This is close to a direct match rather than a stretch -- three of OpenEvo's nine content anchors were built around exactly this theoretical territory before this policy window existed.

fachlicheKlaerung.justification: Evolved cooperation/institution theory is mainstream evolutionary anthropology, not a loose analogy -- well supported in the literature this ecosystem's own TheoryBase/ LiteratureBase already draws on.

schuelervorstellungen.justification: Plausible that students hold a naive "cooperation is just being nice" preconception this connection could productively disrupt, but this repo has not identified a specific, documented study of NY students' own preconceptions about civic cooperation specifically -- rated moderate rather than strong pending that check.

didaktischeStrukturierung.justification: A concrete classroom structure exists (see bridgingActivity) but has not been piloted; whether it fits realistically inside a capstone or CTE-pathway time budget is untested.

content.evidenceMethod: Direct comparison of the Global Citizen attribute's own official wording and NYKids' published elaboration against OpenEvo's existing content-anchor descriptions (from this ecosystem's own content-anchor-mapper/design-concept-coach skills), looking for attributes whose official language already gestures at a mechanism OpenEvo's anchors make explicit.
content.bridgingActivity: A Payoff Matrices exercise modeling a real local or global commons problem (e.g. a shared resource, a public-goods scenario relevant to a school's own community) alongside a Causal Mapping exercise tracing how reputation and third-party enforcement stabilize cooperation in that scenario -- structured as capstone-eligible evidence for the Global Citizen attribute specifically.
content.gaps: Learner-preconception research specific to NY students is not yet identified (see schuelervorstellungen above); this connection has not been reviewed by anyone besides the person who proposed it.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft candidate, not yet reviewed by a second party.
provenance.sourceProvenance: https://ny-kids.org/enhancing-citizenship-skills-with-new-york-states-portrait-of-a-graduate/ (fetched 2026-09-11); OpenEvo content-anchor vocabulary per curriculum-agents' content-anchor-mapper/thinking-tools-kit skill descriptions, live in this session.

nys-lpm.title: Offer ready-made rubric infrastructure for the evidence gap NYSED has already named, not new infrastructure from scratch

content.label: Offer ready-made rubric infrastructure for the evidence gap NYSED has already named, not new infrastructure from scratch
content.statement: NYSED's June 2026 competency-based-diploma announcement commits to "statewide performance standards and common rubrics" that do not yet exist, for evidence pathways (capstones, interdisciplinary project-based learning, CTE programs) that are already named and already official. OpenEvo's existing competency infrastructure -- ConceptBase's structured competency definitions, and the assessment-designer pattern that generates a paired AI-scorable and unplugged (paper/facilitator-run) instrument with a shared scoring rubric from the same underlying item bank -- is a working answer to exactly this named, dated, still-open gap. The right offer is not "adopt our curriculum" but "here is a piloted rubric instrument for one capstone-eligible topic, built the way your own announcement says evidence should be scored."
content.rationale: This is the single most concrete, least speculative point of leverage this research found: it responds to NYSED's own words, not to an inferred need. It also directly answers the Fordham Institute's substantive critique (NYLP-ACTOR-fordham-institute-ny) by demonstrating rigor rather than arguing against the criticism abstractly.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed.

nys-lpm.title: Map OpenEvo's content anchors directly onto the Portrait's attributes as ready-to-use content, not a competing framework

content.label: Map OpenEvo's content anchors directly onto the Portrait's attributes as ready-to-use content, not a competing framework
content.statement: OpenEvo's nine content anchors and six thinking tools already supply concrete, field-tested interdisciplinary material for exactly the Portrait attributes schools now have to find evidence for. Cooperation Games, Governing the Commons, and Global Sustainability Goals map directly onto Global Citizen ("acts responsibly and ethically in local, global, and digital communities"). Tinbergen's Questions and Causal Mapping map onto Critical Thinker. Analogy Mapping and Structure of Knowledge Diagrams map onto Creative Innovator. Presented correctly, this is not "please also do OpenEvo's thing" -- it is "here is fully-built content for the thing you already have to do."
content.rationale: Districts and school leaders under a new, still-underspecified requirement are more receptive to ready-made content that visibly reduces their own workload than to a new framework asking for more of it -- the same framing risk deutsche_lp's own Sachsen principle (DELP-PRINCIPLE-sachsen-curriculum-coherence-analysis) identified independently in a completely different governance system, which is itself worth citing as convergent evidence when making this pitch.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed.

nys-lpm.title: Use SCDN's existing quarterly-meeting structure as the statewide distribution channel, not district-by-district outreach

content.label: Use SCDN's existing quarterly-meeting structure as the statewide distribution channel, not district-by-district outreach
content.statement: The Staff and Curriculum Development Network (SCDN) already convenes instructional leaders from all 37 BOCES and the Big 5 Cities four times a year, already lists Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education, Civic Readiness, and Social-Emotional Learning as current focus areas, and has already shared PreK-5 Portrait-integration resources. One relationship with SCDN -- a session proposal, a piece shared into a Collaborative Group -- reaches instructional leadership across most of the state at once, rather than requiring separate relationships with individual districts or BOCES.
content.rationale: Directly mirrors deutsche_lp's own finding that Sachsen's Projektgruppe Bildungsland 2030 (DELP-ACTOR-smk-projektgruppe-bildungsland-2030) is "the most direct institutional entry point" for that state's reform -- both repos independently arrived at the same strategic shape (find the one coordinating body already doing the convening work, rather than building new relationships from zero), despite Germany and New York having almost nothing in common institutionally. See docs/strategy/2026-09-11-cross-context-comparison-with-deutsche-lp.md.

provenance.contributor_notes: SCDN's own structure/mission facts are sourced at primary-source-confirmed via nysscdn.org (see NYLP-ACTOR-scdn's provenance) but were not independently re-fetched by direct WebFetch this session -- verify directly before this principle is acted on as an outreach plan, not just a research finding.

nys-lpm.title: All New York outreach runs as GlobalESD-and-OpenEvo cooperation, not OpenEvo acting alone

content.label: All New York outreach runs as GlobalESD-and-OpenEvo cooperation, not OpenEvo acting alone
content.statement: Every brief, pilot, and outreach action this repo proposes for New York should be framed as cooperation between GlobalESD (OpenEvo's nonprofit partner, globalesd.org) and OpenEvo's content/research infrastructure -- GlobalESD is the nonprofit vehicle making the offer; OpenEvo's content anchors, thinking tools, and rubric infrastructure are what it brings to the table. This is a standing structural rule for this repo, not a one-off framing choice: no brief, email draft, or pitch built from this repo's records should introduce "OpenEvo" or "the lab" as an unaffiliated actor.
content.rationale: GlobalESD's own existing programs -- Educational Design Labs (interdisciplinary curriculum via teacher capacity building) and School-based Community Science Labs (student/community improvement-project teams) -- are close enough to what a Portrait-aligned capstone pilot needs that GlobalESD is a genuine fit, not a formality attached after the fact. A named, registered nonprofit with existing ESD programming is also a more credible first point of contact for a school or BOCES than an unbranded research-lab identity would be on its own.

provenance.contributor_notes: Added 2026-09-11 per Dustin's direct, explicit instruction mid-session: "ensure this work in NYS is always in cooperation with our Non-profit partner, GlobalESD." Status set to "adopted" rather than "proposed" or "draft" because this is a standing instruction already in force, not a recommendation awaiting a decision.

nys-lpm.title: Treat the strongest public critique of the Portrait as the target to satisfy, not an obstacle to route around

content.label: Treat the strongest public critique of the Portrait as the target to satisfy, not an obstacle to route around
content.statement: The Fordham Institute's critique -- vague standards, no common rubrics, inconsistent teacher-by-teacher scoring, loss of statewide accountability -- is a real, substantive, publicly visible risk, not noise to ignore while pitching interdisciplinary content. A piloted capstone or CTE-pathway unit that is both genuinely interdisciplinary (multiple content anchors, a real integrating question) AND rigorously, consistently scorable (a shared rubric, an AI-scorable instrument validated against an unplugged facilitator-run version) is a direct answer to the critique's strongest form, and a more credible calling card with skeptical school leaders than material that only engages audiences already enthusiastic about the Portrait.
content.rationale: A strategy that only talks to the Portrait's supporters risks looking like advocacy rather than substance to exactly the cautious, accountability-minded administrators (the kind NYSSBA and NYSED's own Commissioner voiced timeline concerns as) whose buy-in actually determines whether a pilot gets a second year.

provenance.contributor_notes: First-draft policy principle, not yet reviewed.

nys-lpm.title: The Portrait's own attribute list changed between the 2024 draft and 2025 adoption

content.label: The Portrait's own attribute list changed between the 2024 draft and 2025 adoption

objects.excerptText: Critical Thinker / Innovative Problem Solver / Literate Across the Content Areas / Cultural Competence / Social-Emotional Competence / Effective Communicator / Global Citizen (seven-part wheel, 'NEW YORK STATE PORTRAIT OF A GRADUATE')
objects.sourceDocument: New York State Graduation Measures Initiative: A Transformational Vision (Board of Regents Update, June 2024)

objects.excerptText: Academically Prepared / Creative Innovator / Critical Thinker / Effective Communicator / Global Citizen / Reflective and Future-Focused -- six interconnected attributes, all grounded in Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education
objects.sourceDocument: Chalkbeat: 'NY approves portrait of a graduate as Regents exams are...'

content.summary: Between the June 2024 draft (a seven-attribute wheel) and the July 2025 adopted framework (six attributes), the Portrait's own structure changed: "Innovative Problem Solver" appears to have been renamed to "Creative Innovator"; "Literate Across the Content Areas" was dropped as a standalone attribute (likely folded into "Academically Prepared"); "Cultural Competence" and "Social-Emotional Competence" no longer appear as peer attributes at all -- they appear to have been absorbed into the framework's foundational Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education layer rather than surviving as individually-named, individually-assessed attributes.
content.policyRelevance: This matters for OpenEvo's own strategy in two ways. First, it shows the Portrait's language is not yet fully stable even after formal adoption -- a policy brief citing "the six attributes" should date its source and expect further drift, not treat the current wording as permanent. Second, and more interesting: folding Cultural Competence and Social-Emotional Competence into a foundational layer rather than keeping them as separate, individually-scored attributes is itself a design decision with a real analogue in OpenEvo's own architecture -- content anchors and thinking tools are not scored as independent add-ons either, but woven through every unit via the three design principles. Worth citing this parallel directly when explaining OpenEvo's design concept to a NYSED or SCDN audience: "you already made this move once, at the level of your own six attributes."
content.exhaustivenessCaveat: Based on directly reading both the June 2024 PDF (all 10 pages) and the July 2025 Chalkbeat article this session -- not a systematic search for an intermediate draft that might show the transition more gradually. The 2024-11 "NY Inspires" announcement (see NYLP-EVENT-ny-inspires-plan-announced) may contain an intermediate version not checked here.

provenance.sourceProvenance: Both source documents read/fetched directly 2026-09-11; see objects[] above for the specific URLs.

Rather than a vague "state hasn't figured it out yet," this finding pins the gap to a specific, dated, still-open commitment NYSED made to itself. It is also the single clearest concrete opening for OpenEvo's own assessment-design work (the EvoFlex-pattern AI-scorable-plus-unplugged instrument approach, and ConceptBase's already-structured competency definitions) to offer something NYSED does not yet have, rather than something redundant with existing state work.

content.role: 37 regional public agencies across New York State providing shared educational services to component school districts -- collectively cover nearly the entire state outside the "Big 5" city districts (NYC, Buffalo, Rochester, Syracuse, Yonkers). nys-lpm.title: Staff and Curriculum Development Network (SCDN / NY S/CDN)

content.label: Staff and Curriculum Development Network (SCDN / NY S/CDN)
content.role: Self-governing instructional-leadership arm of the 37 BOCES and the "Big 5" Cities, operating since 1986 (originally SED-funded, now self-sustaining under its own by-laws). Mission: "strengthen the capacity of school districts to promote successful attainment of the New York State Standards by all students." Members meet quarterly (1.5-day sessions: learning sessions, regional conversations, partnership time with NYSED). Current stated focus areas -- Diversity Equity and Inclusion, Culturally Responsive and Sustaining Education, Civic Readiness, and Social-Emotional Learning -- map directly onto the Portrait of a Graduate's own CR-S Education foundation and its Global Citizen and Reflective-and-Future-Focused attributes. Already shared PreK-5 Portrait-integration resources and hosted regional implementation discussions as of mid-2026. This is the single most promising real distribution channel this research identified: one relationship with SCDN's quarterly-meeting structure could reach instructional leaders across most of the state's districts, not just one.

nys-lpm.title: NYS Portrait of a Graduate (adopted framework)

content.label: NYS Portrait of a Graduate (adopted framework)
content.issuingBody: New York State Board of Regents
content.statementText: "A unifying vision of what it means to be a graduate in New York State... describing the essential skills and dispositions that all students should develop to be successful in college, careers, and civic life." Six attributes -- Academically Prepared, Creative Innovator, Critical Thinker, Effective Communicator, Global Citizen, Reflective and Future-Focused -- all grounded in Culturally Responsive-Sustaining Education. "All students must demonstrate proficiency in each component of the Portrait of a Graduate to earn a high school diploma."

provenance.contributor_notes: The six-attribute list and adoption date are corroborated independently by Chalkbeat (2025-07-14) and by aggregated search results citing WBNG/WWNY local news (2026-05-07) -- the strongest-corroborated fact in this repo's founding session. The attribute NAMES themselves are not identical to the June 2024 seven-attribute draft wheel -- see NYLP-FINDING-portrait-attribute-consolidation-2024-to-2025.

nys-lpm.title: "First-in-the-nation" competency-based diploma direction

content.label: "First-in-the-nation" competency-based diploma direction
content.issuingBody: New York State Education Department (NYSED) and Board of Regents, jointly
content.statementText: "This work represents a bold reimagining of what education can and should be. It challenges long-held assumptions about how learning is measured." (Chancellor Lester W. Young, Jr.) "New York is leading the nation by ensuring that a diploma represents something meaningful, a demonstrated readiness for opportunities." (Commissioner Betty A. Rosa) Students will demonstrate readiness through "evidence of learning developed over time," including "career-connected learning, interdisciplinary project-based learning, and capstone projects," assessed against "statewide performance standards and common rubrics" (not yet published as of this record's date) rather than standardized tests alone.

provenance.contributor_notes: This is this repo's single most important mandate record for OpenEvo's own strategy: it is the one place NYSED's own language explicitly names "interdisciplinary project-based learning" as an official evidence pathway, and explicitly commits to "common rubrics" that do not yet exist -- directly where rigorous, pre-built competency/rubric infrastructure (this ecosystem's own ConceptBase + assessment-designer pattern) has something concrete to offer. Status is deliberately "proposed", not "adopted": as of 2026-09-11 this is a stated direction with quoted officials, not yet a finalized binding credit/graduation rule the way the 2025-07-14 Portrait adoption or the Regents-exam sunset are.

nys-lpm.title: Regents exam / +1 Pathway Assessment requirement removed as diploma gate

india-lpm.title: Ministry of Education, Government of India

content.label: Ministry of Education, Government of India
content.role: The central government ministry that NCERT and CBSE both operate under (as "autonomous" bodies, per NCERT's own description of its relationship to the Ministry). Oversees national implementation of the National Education Policy (NEP) 2020.

provenance.contributor_notes: Basic institutional-hierarchy fact (Ministry oversees NCERT/CBSE), confirmed via dsel.education.gov.in (an official Ministry of Education subdomain) and cross-checked against NCERT's and CBSE's own "autonomous body" self-descriptions.

india-lpm.title: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)

content.label: National Council of Educational Research and Training (NCERT)
content.legalForm: registered society under the Societies Registration Act, 1860 (Act XXI) -- not a government department itself, though set up by the Government of India in 1961 and described as autonomous under the Ministry of Education
content.role: Prepares the National Curriculum Framework (most recently NCF 2023, under NEP 2020, covering ages 3-18) and publishes India's standard national textbooks. Also actively asserts and enforces copyright over its own textbook and curriculum-framework text: its own state-adoption license agreement states "The NCERT is the sole owner of copyright of the WORK" and that copyright "shall vest with the NCERT in perpetuity," and NCERT has publicly warned that unauthorized reproduction "will face legal action under the Copyright Act 1957." This repo's own founding research found NCERT's legal-society status (rather than being a literal government department) leaves it a genuinely open question whether Copyright Act 1957 Section 2(k)'s "government work" provision applies to its output by plain statutory text -- see docs/source-notes/2026-09-30-india-curriculum-licensing-landscape-research.md#2 for the unresolved-legal-question flag.

provenance.contributor_notes: The quoted license-agreement language ("sole owner... in perpetuity") was read directly from NCERT's own state-adoption license agreement PDF, not a secondary summary. The legal-form/registered-society fact is corroborated by three independent sources (Vajiram & Ravi, understandupsc.com, Wikipedia) in the research session, none of which is itself a primary NCERT document -- flagging that the legal-form claim rests on secondary characterization even though the license-text quote is primary.

india-lpm.title: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)

content.label: Central Board of Secondary Education (CBSE)
content.legalForm: autonomous body registered under the Societies Registration Act, 1860, under the Ministry of Education -- not a government department itself
content.role: Sets curricula/syllabi for its affiliated schools nationwide and administers board exams. Search-engine excerpts of CBSE's own curriculum PDFs (cbseacademic.nic.in) suggest they carry a reproduction-restriction notice similar in spirit to NCERT's, but this repo's founding session could not independently confirm that specific wording by reading a CBSE PDF directly -- treat the reproduction-notice claim as likely-but-unverified until a future session reads one directly.

provenance.contributor_notes: The basic institutional facts (autonomous society, sets national curricula, under Ministry of Education) are confirmed via dsel.education.gov.in (an official government page) and corroborated by Wikipedia. The specific reproduction-notice wording attributed to CBSE curriculum PDFs was found only via search-engine excerpt, not a PDF read directly this session -- see role field's own caveat.

india-lpm.title: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India

content.label: Ministry of Tribal Affairs, Government of India
content.role: The central ministry that runs the Eklavya Model Residential School (EMRS) scheme -- added to this repo as part of its first Kerala- tribal-education research pass (2026-10-09) because EMRS operates two schools inside Kerala (EMRS Pookode, Wayanad, established 1997; EMRS Painavu, Idukki) run on the Jawahar Navodaya Vidyalaya model, funded under Article 275(1) of the Constitution, targeted at blocks with over 50% Scheduled Tribe population and at least 20,000 tribal persons. india-lpm.title: NCERT/CIET launch NROER under CC BY-SA, later inactive

content.label: NCERT/CIET launch NROER under CC BY-SA, later inactive
content.description: NCERT/CIET launched the National Repository of Open Educational Resources (NROER) in August 2013, defaulting its hosted resources to a CC BY-SA license -- a real, if narrower, precedent for NCERT publishing under an open license, in real tension with the all-rights-reserved language in NCERT's own state-adoption agreement (see INLP-EVENT-ncert-license-agreement-perpetual-copyright). The repository appears now inactive; no precise retirement date was found. A follow-up review of Karnataka's KOER (see state/karnataka/local_policy/records/timeline.yaml) found that NROER's own hosting was itself incomplete -- several chapters missing -- even during its active period.

india-lpm.title: Karnataka's own Class 10 Science 'Heredity' chapter is openly licensed; the national default is not

content.label: Karnataka's own Class 10 Science 'Heredity' chapter is openly licensed; the national default is not

objects.subject: Science
objects.excerptText: Hybridisation is the process of combining different varieties of an organism to create a hybrid.
objects.licenseOrRightsNote: KOER states directly, on its own "Brief note on KOER" page, that its content is licensed under Creative Commons Attribution-ShareAlike 4.0 International (CC BY-SA 4.0) -- confirmed by two independent direct fetches (this repo's founding session, 2026-09-30, and again 2026-10-02). Safe to quote verbatim on that basis.

content.summary: Karnataka's own Class 10 Science textbook, as mirrored on KOER, covers heredity at Chapter 21 -- a different number from NCERT's own similarly-named national chapter, which this repo has not directly re-confirmed this session (see exhaustivenessCaveat) -- and does so under an explicit, checkable open license. NCERT's own curriculum text, by contrast, defaults to all-rights-reserved across the board (see national_ccs_policy/records/institutional-actors.yaml, INLP-ACTOR-ncert, and docs/source-notes/2026-09-30-india-curriculum-licensing-landscape-research.md#3). The same underlying school-science topic therefore sits at two genuinely different redistribution-rights tiers depending on which jurisdiction's own version of it is in hand -- a concrete, specific instance of the state-to-state (and state-to-national) licensing variation this repo's founding research already found in the abstract, now anchored to one real, named chapter rather than stated only as a general pattern.
content.policyRelevance: Demonstrates the accessTier/licenseOrRightsNote model doing real work: the same curriculum topic can be stored at a materially higher tier in one jurisdiction's records than another, for a stated, real, checkable reason, with neither tier being an accident of effort rather than law.
content.exhaustivenessCaveat: Two honest limits, so this finding isn't overclaimed. First: this repo has not directly re-confirmed NCERT's own current Class 10 Science chapter numbering/title this session (its all-rights-reserved default is independently well-sourced elsewhere in this repo, but the specific "different chapter number" comparison rests on general background knowledge, not a fresh primary-source check) -- treat the NCERT side of this comparison as plausible, not verified, until someone reads NCERT's current textbook directly. Second, and more important: KOER's own CC BY-SA licensing is real and confirmed, but the wiki page behind this specific chapter is, as of 2026-10-02, a thin structural stub -- a short definition plus outbound links, not a fully-authored treatment -- and a same-session check of the most likely adjacent human-origins page (Class 8 Social Science, "Geographical Features And Pre-Historic India") found the same thing. Open licensing and content maturity are different axes; this finding is about the first, not a claim about the second.

provenance.contributor_notes: excerptText and the license claim were both read directly from koer-en.karnatakaeducation.org.in's own live pages this session, independent of (and consistent with) the founding session's 2026-09-30 licensing research. The NCERT-side chapter-numbering comparison is this record's one unverified claim -- see exhaustivenessCaveat -- and should be checked directly before this finding is cited in anything leaving this repo (a brief, outreach, or an exported public example repo).

Safe to quote verbatim on that basis.

india-lpm.title: Department of State Educational Research and Training (DSERT), Karnataka

content.label: Department of State Educational Research and Training (DSERT), Karnataka
content.role: Karnataka's state curriculum-research body. Runs Karnataka Open Educational Resources (KOER), which licenses the state's own textbooks and curriculum materials under Creative Commons CC BY-SA 4.0 -- a real, checkable, already-open license, in direct contrast to NCERT's own all-rights-reserved default (see national_ccs_policy/records/institutional-actors.yaml, INLP-ACTOR-ncert) and to Maharashtra's fee-gated approach (see state/maharashtra/local_policy/records/institutional-actors.yaml, INLP-ACTOR-balbharati-maharashtra). Karnataka's DSERT has also set up its own curriculum-design expert bodies partly independent of national NCF/NEP 2020 content, reflecting India's constitutional "Concurrent List" status for education, which lets states diverge both in curriculum content and in licensing posture.

provenance.contributor_notes: The CC BY-SA 4.0 licensing claim and the "hosted in full, unlike NROER" comparison both come from a SpicyIP legal-scholarship piece (Dhonchak, 2021), corroborated by the KOER portal itself, which this repo's founding session viewed directly. The "own curriculum design expert bodies" / NEP-divergence claim comes from an ORF policy-analysis piece, a secondary source -- flagged as somewhat less certain than the licensing claim itself.

india-lpm.title: IT for Change

content.label: IT for Change
content.role: Bangalore-based NGO that served as DSERT's resource/implementation partner in building Karnataka Open Educational Resources (KOER) under the national RMSA Karnataka (Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan) scheme, 2013-14 -- designed the cascading teacher-training model that produced KOER's own content (see state/karnataka/local_policy/records/timeline.yaml, INLP-EVENT-koer-rmsa-pilot-launch). Recorded here as its own actor, distinct from DSERT itself (INLP-ACTOR-dsert-karnataka), because the content-creation mechanism -- a civil-society partner training a cascading chain of teachers, rather than the state board authoring material centrally -- is a structurally different model from how Maharashtra's Balbharati or NCERT itself produce curriculum content, and that difference is part of what makes KOER's open-license posture possible in practice, not just on paper.

provenance.contributor_notes: Confirmed by a direct fetch of KOER's own "Brief note on KOER" page, which names IT for Change as the resource institution and describes the RMSA Karnataka-funded cascading training model (30 core teachers per subject across 19 districts, training roughly 30 more each, who then trained teachers at roughly 1,000 high schools) directly.

india-lpm.title: KOER launches as a Class-IX-only pilot under RMSA Karnataka, then grows

content.label: KOER launches as a Class-IX-only pilot under RMSA Karnataka, then grows
content.description: DSERT built Karnataka Open Educational Resources (KOER) with IT for Change as resource/implementation partner, under the national RMSA (Rashtriya Madhyamik Shiksha Abhiyan) secondary-education scheme. Deliberately scoped at launch to Class IX topics only, in Mathematics, Science, and Social Science, in English and Kannada -- built via a cascading teacher-training model (roughly 30 "core" teachers per subject across 19 districts, each training roughly 30 more, who in turn trained teachers at roughly 1,000 high schools), with an explicit stated goal to expand to all classes, subjects, and media of instruction over time.
